name: Luteolin (alone and in combination products)
short: With quercetin and rutin: irritability for 1 to 8 weeks in 27 of 50 autistic children. Alone: no adverse events in 5 men with prostate cancer. With palmitoylethanolamide: none in a 202-person trial.
text: Human safety data on luteolin are limited, and most come from combination products taken by mouth, whose harms cannot be credited to luteolin alone. Luteolin alone: in a single-arm phase I study without a control group, 5 men aged 60 to 78 with low-to-intermediate-risk prostate cancer under active surveillance took luteolin by mouth daily for 6 months, and no adverse events were noted in any of them; two of the five had disease progression and then had surgery, and the abstract does not say whether this was related to luteolin. In a 26-week open-label study in 50 children aged 4 to 10 with autism spectrum disorder given a dietary supplement containing luteolin, quercetin and rutin in olive kernel oil, 27 of the 50 had transiently increased irritability lasting 1 to 8 weeks, and 40 completed the study; the authors report no major adverse effects. In an uncontrolled case series of 37 children with autism spectrum disorder aged 4 to 14 who used a similar luteolin, quercetin and rutin formulation in olive kernel oil for at least 4 months, no adverse effects were reported. With palmitoylethanolamide (the combination used for loss of smell after COVID-19): in a blinded, placebo-controlled randomised trial in 202 people with persistent smell loss, in which one of four groups took placebo with smell training, all completed and there were no adverse events; in a 6-month randomised trial in 85 people with parosmia, all treatment regimens were well tolerated; and a 185-person placebo-controlled trial of the oral supplement gives no adverse-event data in its abstract. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
